claim: Adult male worms undergo spermatogenesis, while adult hermaphrodite worms undergo oogenesis.
source: Adult male worms undergo spermatogenesis, while adult hermaphrodite worms undergo oogenesis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and illustrated in Figure 1A showing the organization of hermaphrodite and male germlines.

claim: The germline for both sexes is organized as a spatial-temporal gradient along the distal-proximal axis.
source: The germline for both sexes is organized as a spatial-temporal gradient along the distal-proximal axis, thereby allowing for easy and simultaneous access to all stages of meiotic prophase I (Gartner and Engebrecht, 2022; Hillers et al., 2017).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The SC initiates assembly late in the transition zone (leptotene/zygotene) and is fully assembled by pachytene.
source: The SC initiates assembly late in the transition zone (leptotene/zygotene) and is fully assembled by pachytene (MacQueen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by a citation to MacQueen et al., 2002.

claim: Six SYP proteins (SYP-1–SYP-6) span the gap between the homologous chromosomes in the C. elegans SC.
source: While many proteins have been identified within the C. elegans SC, we focused our analyses here on the central region proteins, which are all called SYP (SYnaPsis protein) and, to date, six SYP proteins (SYP-1–SYP-6) span the gap between the homologous chromosomes (Figure 1B; Colaiácovo et al., 2003; Hurlock et al., 2020; MacQueen et al., 2002; Smolikov et al., 2007a; Smolikov et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with supporting citations and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: SYP-2 dynamics are higher in spermatocytes compared to oocytes throughout pachytene.
source: For GFP::SYP-2, spermatocytes displayed significantly higher recovery dynamics throughout pachytene compared to oocytes (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2; p<0.001, Bonferroni–Dunn adjusted, Mann–Whitney).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 1C and supplementary figures.

claim: mCherry::SYP-3 recovered more quickly in oocytes during early pachytene compared to spermatocytes.
source: In contrast, mCherry::SYP-3 recovered more quickly in oocytes during early pachytene compared to spermatocytes (early pachytene p=0.0015; Bonferroni–Dunn adjusted, Mann–Whitney).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with statistical support.

claim: During mid and late pachytene, SYP-3 recovery rates were similar between the sexes.
source: During mid and late pachytene, SYP-3 recovery rates were similar between the sexes.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text.

claim: The progressive stabilization of spermatocyte SYP-3 was less pronounced and more subtle than that of oocyte SYP-3.
source: Notably, we observed that the progressive stabilization of spermatocyte SYP-3 was less pronounced and more subtle than that of oocyte SYP-3, suggesting that spermatocytes may not modulate SYP-3 stability via the same mechanisms as oocytes (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Both sexes showed the same overall trend of progressive stabilization of SYP-2 and SYP-3 throughout pachytene.
source: Overall, both sexes showed the same overall trend of progressive stabilization of SYP-2 and SYP-3 throughout pachytene, matching previous observations with the transgene GFP::SYP-3 (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2; see 'Methods'; Nadarajan et al., 2017; Pattabiraman et al., 2017; Rog et al., 2017).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with supporting citations and reference to figures.

claim: In oocytes, GFP::SYP-2 turnover was significantly reduced compared to mCherry::SYP-3 turnover.
source: In oocytes, GFP::SYP-2 turnover was significantly reduced compared to mCherry::SYP-3 turnover (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2; p<0.01, Bonferroni–Dunn adjusted, Mann–Whitney).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with statistical support and reference to figures.

claim: In spermatocytes, only early pachytene displayed significant differences in GFP::SYP-2 and mCherry::SYP-3 turnover.
source: Comparatively in spermatocytes, only early pachytene displayed significant differences in GFP::SYP-2 and mCherry::SYP-3 turnover (Figure 1C; p=0.0237, Bonferroni–Dunn adjusted, Mann–Whitney).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with statistical support and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: SYP-2 and SYP-3 can be independently regulated during pachytene.
source: These results demonstrate that SYP-2 and SYP-3 can be independently regulated during pachytene.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: SC length was similar throughout pachytene in each sex.
source: Our results found that SC length was similar throughout pachytene in each sex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The slightly shorter SC lengths in late pachytene spermatocytes were likely due to differences in chromosome compaction between the sexes.
source: The slightly shorter SC lengths in late pachytene spermatocytes were likely due to differences in chromosome compaction between the sexes (Rourke and Jaramillo-Lambert, 2022; Samson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with supporting citations.

claim: Independent regulation of SYP-2 and SYP-3 within an assembled SC is not due to changes in chromosome length.
source: These results suggest that independent regulation of SYP-2 and SYP-3 within an assembled SC is not due to changes in chromosome length, but rather by other factors.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the SC length measurements.

claim: The accumulation of GFP::SYP-2 in the SC is sexually dimorphic.
source: We found that the accumulation of GFP::SYP-2 in the SC is sexually dimorphic (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with reference to Figure 2A and B.

claim: Wild-type oocytes progressively accumulated SYP-2 up until the early to mid pachytene transition.
source: Wild-type oocytes progressively accumulated SYP-2 up until the early to mid pachytene transition (early pachytene mean intensity 153,292.27 ± SD 13,983.85; early/mid pachytene mean peak intensity 161,878.14± SD 13,930.43; mid pachytene mean intensity 148,430.1± SD 13,058.02) and then reduce the amount of SYP-2 slightly before maintaining a relatively constant level of SYP-2 through late pachytene.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with quantitative data.

claim: Wild-type spermatocytes progressively loaded SYP-2 into the SC until the onset of late pachytene at which point the amount of SYP-2 began to stabilize.
source: In contrast to oocytes, wild-type spermatocytes progressively loaded SYP-2 into the SC until the onset of late pachytene at which point the amount of SYP-2 began to stabilize (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with reference to Figure 2A and B.

claim: Early pachytene spermatocytes had less SYP-2 loaded than oocytes, but late pachytene spermatocytes had near or slightly more amounts of SYP-2 in the SC than oocytes.
source: Notably, early pachytene spermatocytes had less SYP-2 loaded than oocytes, but late pachytene spermatocytes had near or slightly more amounts of SYP-2 in the SC than oocytes (p<0.001, Bonferroni adjusted, Mann–Whitney).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with statistical support.

claim: Only oocytes display a few persisting bright nuclei in nearly all germlines examined at the early/mid pachytene transition of SYP-2 intensity.
source: Additionally, slightly past the early/mid pachytene transition of SYP-2 intensity, we noted only oocytes display a few persisting bright nuclei in nearly all germlines examined (eight out of nine germlines with persisting bright nuclei; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with quantitative observation and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The incorporation of SYP-2 throughout pachytene differs between sexes.
source: Thus, the incorporation of SYP-2 throughout pachytene differs between sexes.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: mCherry::SYP-3 progressively accumulated throughout pachytene in both sexes.
source: In contrast to SYP-2, mCherry::SYP-3 progressively accumulated throughout pachytene in both sexes, matching previous observations using a GFP::SYP-3 transgene (Figure 2C and D; Pattabiraman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with supporting citation and reference to Figure 2C and D.

claim: Differences in fluorescent tags on SYP-3 do not appear to largely influence the incorporation of SYP-3 into the SC during pachytene.
source: Therefore, differences in fluorescent tags on SYP-3 do not appear to largely influence the incorporation of SYP-3 into the SC during pachytene (see 'Methods').
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from comparing mCherry::SYP-3 and GFP::SYP-3.

claim: Spermatocytes incorporated less SYP-3 throughout pachytene compared to oocytes.
source: In comparison to oocytes, spermatocytes incorporated less SYP-3 throughout pachytene (p<0.001, Bonferroni adjusted, Mann–Whitney), which was also observed in the early regions of pachytene with SYP-2.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with statistical support.

claim: Spermatocytes have less SYP-3 and SYP-2 in the SC than oocytes, specifically within the early and mid regions of pachytene.
source: Thus, spermatocytes have less SYP-3 and SYP-2 in the SC than oocytes, specifically within the early and mid regions of pachytene.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Bright SYP-2 nuclei may have defects or changes that only trigger a response with SYP-2 levels.
source: Moreover, unlike with SYP-2, we did not observe in either sex any bright SYP-3 nuclei that were not surrounded by other nuclei of similar intensity, thereby suggesting that these bright SYP-2 nuclei may have defects or changes that only trigger a response with SYP-2 levels (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as an inference from the observation with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: SYP-2 and SYP-3 are differentially incorporated in the SC both over the course of meiotic prophase I and between sexes.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that SYP-2 and SYP-3 are differentially incorporated in the SC both over the course of meiotic prophase I and between sexes.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: SPO-11-induced DSBs are formed in the context of fully assembled SC in early pachytene in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, SPO-11-induced DSBs are formed in the context of fully assembled SC in early pachytene, and these breaks get repaired as the nuclei traverse through pachytene (Gartner and Engebrecht, 2022).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with a supporting citation.

source: By the transition to late pachytene, crossover recombination events are designated and marked by the pro-crossover protein COSA-1 (Yokoo et al., 2012).

source: Additionally, western blot whole worm analysis of GFP::SYP-2 protein showed a slight, but not statistically significant, increase in SYP-2 protein levels in only oocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).

claim: Oocytes and spermatocytes differentially regulate the amount of SYP-2 protein in the absence of DSBs.
source: Thus, oocytes and spermatocytes differentially regulate the amount of SYP-2 protein in the absence of DSBs.
evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that the incorporation of SYPs is regulated in a recombination-dependent and sex-specific manner during prophase I.

source: Specifically, cosa-1 oocytes did not increase the levels of SYP-2 and SYP-3 to the same amounts as observed in spo-11 oocytes (Figure 3).

evidence: This is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

source: In oocytes, reducing the dosage of SYP-1, SYP-2, or SYP-3 by 60–70% was sufficient to permit SC assembly and crossover designation (Libuda et al., 2013).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with a supporting citation.

source: In syp-2/+ and syp-3/+ mutants, the transition zone (determined by DAPI-stained DNA morphology) was not significantly extended in either sex, indicating that chromosome pairing is not impaired by SYP dosage (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

source: SC assembly and/or the maintenance of full-length SC were altered by reducing the dosage of SYP-2 only in oocytes (Figure 4).

claim: In early pachytene, syp-2/+ oocytes displayed more discontinuities in the SC along the chromosomes than both wild type and syp-3/+, suggesting that there is an SC assembly or maintenance defect in syp-2/+.
source: In early pachytene, syp-2/+ oocytes displayed more discontinuities in the SC along the chromosomes than both wild type and syp-3/+, suggesting that there is an SC assembly or maintenance defect in syp-2/+ (Figure 4A, yellow arrowheads).

source: Thus, SC assembly and/or maintenance only in oocytes are sensitive to SYP-2 dosage during the early stages of pachytene and this defect is not severe enough to trigger synapsis checkpoint activation.

source: Thus, DSB formation and repair are not largely impacted by altering the dosage of SYP-2 or SYP-3.
